question: Should OpenClaw permanently support a plugin SDK capability that can complete a host-bound external verification attempt and thereby authorize an allow decision for a protected tool call?
rationale: The code can constrain the path, but only maintainers can decide whether this authority model, public SDK commitment, and persisted approval-state contract belong in core rather than an external integration-specific design.

options.title: Accept the bounded host-owned contract
options.body: Merge after confirming that external verifier completion is an intended supported plugin capability and that the documented Gateway ownership model is the long-term contract.

options.title: Narrow the contract further
options.body: Keep the PR open while maintainers reduce or redesign the public verifier, grant-store, or completion surfaces before accepting the security boundary.

options.title: Keep it outside core for now
options.body: Pause the PR and require the AgentKit integration to use existing plugin capabilities until a core extension seam is explicitly sponsored.

recommendation.title: Accept the bounded host-owned contract
recommendation.body: Merge after confirming that external verifier completion is an intended supported plugin capability and that the documented Gateway ownership model is the long-term contract.

likelyOwner.reason: This contributor has carried the linked issue and both implementation attempts, so they are the clearest available technical routing contact; final product approval still requires a repository decision-maker.
